thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout detected repeated fallback behavior and eviction churn in us-west-2. Detecting sticky fallback -> region fallback loop. Severity: P1. Pager: Amber (oncall).
Amber: acked. I'm paged, looking now. Which rollout ID?
Benson: that's canary-2026-03-15-v2. We started traffic at 09:02 PST and at ~09:06 we see model variant mismatch errors then fallback to stable variant, which is sticky for sessions and causing route thrashing.
Eli: seeing evictions on the serving pool in us-west-2, pods getting continuously reattached. CPU is fine, but KV cache misses spike and latency > 3s for some requests.
Jaime: customer ops saying a subset of enterprise tenants in APAC see increased 5xx and latency. Not global yet but rising.
Ops-Customer: Confirming: 4 customers reported user-facing errors, ~2.1% of requests failing for those orgs in the last 5m. Impacting chat completions.
Amber: ok triage plan: 1) pause canary rollout 2) force-sticky-routing-disable for affected sessions 3) if needed rollback variant. Anyone object?
Benson: No objection. Pausing now: 
```
# redwoodctl
redwoodctl rollout pause --id canary-2026-03-15-v2 --reason "eviction-fallback-loop"
```
incident-bot: Deploy bot: rollout canary-2026-03-15-v2 paused by Benson at 2839000062.
Eli: I'm going to disable sticky fallback policy for the route group temporarily so the system won't try to rebind sessions to the failed canary. Command: 
```
redwoodctl routing update-policy --route checkout-service --policy fallback:sticky=false --force
```
Amber: done?
Eli: ran at 2839000078. Confirmed policy update propagated to routing mesh.
Benson: logs show immediate reduction in route churn but we still get a backlog of queued requests hitting fallback logic. Posting a log extract: 
```
[09:07:12] warn: fallback triggered for session s-7f4a variant=canary-v2 -> stable-v1
[09:07:12] info: sticky-affinity set for session s-7f4a to stable-v1
[09:07:12] error: eviction-loop detected for grp=us-west-2 pool=dedicated-gpu-3 count=6
[09:07:13] debug: kvcache.miss key=prefix-1234
```
Jaime: good. Any customer-impact mitigation we can push immediately? Can we route affected customer traffic to a regional stable endpoint (eu-central) to avoid degraded us-west-2?
Eli: we can force-region-routing for specific orgs. Doing a scoped override for the 4 impacted org IDs: org-847, org-992, org-201, org-305. Command: 
```
redwoodctl route override --org org-847,org-992,org-201,org-305 --region eu-central-1 --reason "mitigation: avoid us-west-2 fallback loop"
```
Amber: apply that and monitor. Benson, can you check capacity in eu-central-1 before we redirect? We don't want to create a secondary outage.
Benson: eu-central has headroom: ~65% GPU utilization, can take the redirected load. Kicking override now.
incident-bot: Route overrides applied at 2839000099 for org-847,org-992,org-201,org-305.
Ops-Customer: seeing errors drop for org-992 within 90s. Thank you.
Amber: next, we need to understand root cause: why did variant mismatch + sticky fallback cause eviction thrash? Benson/Eli, any hypothesis?
Eli: preliminary: the canary variant had a tokenization change that causes larger KV cache entries for some requests; cache pressure led to frequent GC/evictions in serving pool and the routing mesh kept trying to bind sessions back to canary because sticky fallback was still enabled. Combined with autoscaler reacting to thrash and draining, we got oscillation.
Benson: replicating locally with sampled traces shows sequence-length distribution shifted; can reproduce higher KV growth. Suggest reverting canary model artifact and run smaller alpha.
Jaime: recommend rollback to stable v1 for canary rollout and run a quantized test profile before re-attempt.
Amber: agree. Benson, roll back canary artifact and set rollout to aborted.
Benson: rolling back: 
```
redwoodctl rollout abort --id canary-2026-03-15-v2 --reason "eviction-loop/kvcache regression"
```
incident-bot: Rollout aborted by Benson at 2839000128. Canary traffic drained.
Eli: after abort and disabling sticky fallback, eviction events dropped to baseline within 2 minutes. Latency back to normal for non-impacted orgs.
Amber: good. I'll do a pager summary to SRE rotation and notify affected customers with post-incident note. Jaime, can you own the customer comms?
Jaime: will draft an incident update: cause = canary variant introduced kvcache growth; effect = eviction fallback loop due to sticky fallback policy + region routing thrash; remediation = paused rollout, disabled sticky fallback, targeted region overrides, aborted canary. ETA for customer note in 30m.
Ops-Customer: customers appreciate the quick mitigation, please include mitigation steps and whether re-release is anticipated.
Amber: handoff: I'm going offline in 15 min, Eli taking on-call after me. Eli, summary for next shift: monitor routing churn, confirm sticky fallback stays disabled until variant is validated, keep overrides for orgs for 1h then reevaluate.
Eli: acknowledged, will monitor dashboards and run a quick eval on kvcache metrics with model artifact team.
Benson: follow-ups: run artifact compare, add KV size histogram to preflight checks, add canary traffic cap to prevent >5% traffic until KV profile OK.
Amber: thanks all. I'll close the pager and create a postmortem ticket.
incident-bot: Incident closed to P2 at 2839000179 by Amber — follow-up: create INCIDENT-2839 postmortem and link runbook updates. :white_check_mark:
